CONTENT:
Variant Configuration Planner is a SaaS solution built on SAP IBP and SAP BTP that enables characteristics-based demand and supply planning of configurable products. VC Planner is integrated with S4, ECC and SAP Integrated Business Planning modules.

VC Planner is designed to address the supply chain planning challenges for Variant configurations (configurable products), which are products that can be customized according to the customer's specific requirements within the available options. Planning for configurable products is difficult due to the high number of possible configurations, making it hard to perform demand planning and supply planning.

The purpose of a VC (Variant Configuration) Planner is to manage and optimize the planning processes for configurable products. The VC Planner plays a crucial role in addressing the complexities associated with configurable products and ensuring efficient supply chain operations. Here's how the VC Planner can help in each of the mentioned issues:

  • Demand forecasting: The VC Planner uses historical data, market trends, and customer preferences to forecast demand for various configurations. By analyzing past sales data and customer behavior, the VC Planner can provide more accurate demand forecasts, considering the different options and configurations customers may choose.
  • Complexity in supply planning: The VC Planner assists in managing the complexity of supply planning by considering all the options and configurations, along with their corresponding production requirements. It helps determine the components, and sub-assemblies requirements by analyzing the authorization rules associated with the bill of materials and options.
  • Production planning: The VC Planner streamlines the production planning process for configurable products by sending the most accurate independent requirements to the ERP system, it considers the various configurations and their associated production requirements to create an optimized Customer Independent Requirement.
  • Inventory management: The VC Planner aids in effective inventory management by analyzing demand patterns and production requirements for different configurations. It helps determine the appropriate demand levels for each component and sub-assembly, preventing excess inventory or stockouts. This ensures that companies have the right inventory at the right time, optimizing working capital and reducing holding costs.

Overall, the VC Planner acts as a central coordinating function that leverages technology, data analysis, and expertise to optimize planning processes for configurable products. It helps companies overcome the challenges associated with managing and delivering configurable products effectively.

The scope of the VC Planner software includes the following key features:

  1. Generates master schedule for assemblies: The VC Planner software allows users to generate a master schedule for the production of products and assemblies associated with it. It takes into account the various components and sub-assemblies required for each configuration and helps in creating a master production plan by accurately predicting the demand for each configuration.
  1. Predicts order configurations: The VC Planner software has the capability to predict order configurations based on historical data, customer preferences, and market trends. It helps anticipate the most popular configurations and assists in demand forecasting and production planning.
  1. Supports classic Super BOM / iPPE structures: The VC Planner software supports both classic Super BOM (Bill of Materials) and iPPE (Internet-enabled Product and Process Engineering) structures. This allows for flexible configuration management and enables users to define and manage complex product structures with multiple options and variations.
  1. Planning for assembly line restrictions: The VC Planner software considers assembly line restrictions and constraints during production planning. It provides insights about the limitations of the assembly line, such as capacity constraints, and component / assembly requirements.
  1. New product introduction: The VC Planner software facilitates the planning and introduction of new products. It supports the configuration and planning of new product variants, enabling efficient production ramp-up and smooth integration into the existing production processes.
  1. Version/Scenario planning: The VC Planner software allows users to create different planning versions or scenarios. This feature enables users to compare and analyze various planning scenarios, considering factors such as different demand forecasts, available capacity. It helps in making informed decisions and evaluating the impact of different planning approaches.
  1. Critical component analysis: The VC Planner software provides analysis and visibility into critical components. It identifies components that are essential for multiple configurations and provides insights on the supply of these critical components to avoid production delays or stockouts.
  1. Restriction Planning analysis: The VC Planner software provides visibility into restrictions for different rules on various options. It identifies the likelihood of configurations that are used in multiple products and provides insights on the availability of these configurations.
  1. Integrated with supply chain processes: The VC Planner software is integrated with other processes, such as Demand Planning, Production Scheduling, Sales & Operations Planning. It ensures seamless coordination between planning and execution, allowing for real-time updates and adjustments based on actual sales and inventory levels.

In summary, the scope of the VC Planner software encompasses generating master schedules, predicting order configurations, supporting complex BOM structures, planning for assembly line restrictions, facilitating new product introductions, version/scenario planning, critical component analysis, and seamless integration with execution processes.

The intended audience for this software document includes professionals involved in Supply Chain Management, Master Production Planning, Inventory Management. This may also include:

IT Managers: Professionals responsible for managing the software systems and technology infrastructure supporting the supply chain and production planning processes.

Executives and Decision-makers: Higher-level managers and executives who need a comprehensive understanding of the challenges and strategies related to managing configurable products in the supply chain.

It is important to note that the document can be tailored to suit the specific needs and level of technical understanding of the intended audience. It should provide clear and concise information, explaining the benefits of the VC Planner and how it addresses the challenges faced by the target audience in a language that is accessible to them.

Terminology

Description

VC Planner

Variant Configuration Planner

Configurable Product

A product that can be customized or configured based on various attributes, options, and features.

Variant Configuration

The process of defining and managing the different configurations and options available for a configurable product.

Options Planning

Generating option percentages based on sales orders or seed orders to adjust values and configurations.

Forecast Order Generation

Predicting future demand and generating forecast orders based on configured options.

Assembly Requirements

Identifying the components or assemblies needed to fulfill a specific product configuration.

Restriction Planning

Establishing production constraints for specific characteristic values to validate against capacity.

Master Data

Essential data that defines the characteristics, options, and rules for configuring products.

Characteristics

Distinct attributes or properties that define a product's configuration options.

Seed Orders

Simulated or pseudo sales orders used for generating option percentages and forecasting.

VC Planner offers an array of advanced features designed to enhance the planning process for Configurable Products. The software streamlines planning by providing several key functionalities:

  • Options Planning: For configurable products, VC Planner generates Option Percentages based on Sales Orders or Seed Orders. This automated feature enables planners to adjust values in response to the system's proposed option percentages.
  • Forecast Order Generation: The VC Planning engine generates predictions and Forecast Order Quantities based on the Option Plan. These forecasts serve as Independent Requirements for producing products with specific specifications. Forecast orders are seamlessly integrated into ERP systems like S4 as Customer Independent Requirements.
  • Assembly or Component Requirements: VC Planner generates assembly or component requirements based on predefined rules and object dependencies for configurable products. It also considers market authorizations to populate requirements only for valid combinations and specific time frames.
  • Component Capacity Check: Planners benefit from detailed capacity checks at the component level. VC Planner enables adjustments to Demand or Option mixes, ensuring alignment with capacity constraints at this granular level.
  • Restriction Planning: The software empowers planners to establish production constraints using rule-based systems for defined Characteristic Values. These rules validate requirements against restriction capacities, enhancing accuracy in the planning process.
  • Reports and Analytics: VC Planner boasts an extensive range of reporting and analytical tools tailored for Variant Configuration planning. Its built-in solutions provide insights for analytics and reporting purposes, catering to the diverse needs of planners.
  • Forecast Accuracy: VC Planner includes essential Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) like Forecast Error Measures and Accuracy Calculations. These metrics grant planner's valuable visibility during the monthly planning cycle.
  • Snapshots: VC Planner captures snapshots at different stages, facilitating easy comparison between the latest and current plans. This feature enhances planners' ability to track changes and progress.

VC Planner offers an impressive suite of features that streamline the planning process for Configurable Products. From generating forecasts and managing assembly requirements to capacity checks and detailed reporting, the software provides planners with the tools they need for efficient and accurate planning. Additionally, the ability to capture snapshots and assess forecast accuracy further strengthens planners' decision-making capabilities. VC Planner stands as a comprehensive solution to enhance Variant Configuration planning processes.

Two distinct user roles can be assigned within the system:

    1. Configurator Role

         Users with the "Configurator" role will possess specific access privileges:

    • Access to configure both VCP Configuration and VCP Master Data. This includes defining and fine-tuning various parameters and settings related to configuration and master data.

    2. Planner Role

          Users granted the "Planner" role will have the following access rights:

    • Permission to execute and schedule various jobs that are essential for the planning process.
    • Planners will handle tasks associated with generating plans, running calculations, and ensuring that the planning process progresses as intended.
    • This role is pivotal in orchestrating the planning activities and ensuring they are executed efficiently.

    3. IT Support

         Users granted the "Support" role will have the following access rights:

    • The user will have access to configuration and planner roles application only in display mode.
    • The role is used to backtrack and understand the data by support team

    4. IT Admin

         User granted with "Admin" role will have the following access rights:

    • The user will have access to provide access to other users to make changes in VCP. By default, all the users will have only display authorizations and when the user is added and provide with Create, update, delete and read, Configurator and Planner will have access to modify the data.

The User Interface of the VC Planner system encompasses four distinct systems, each serving specific functions and tasks:

SAP ERP/S4Hana Integration:

The SAP ERP/S4Hana system acts as a primary data source for VC Planner, supplying most of the necessary data.

VC Planner provides standard extractors to seamlessly retrieve data from SAP ERP/S4Hana, ensuring a reliable and continuous flow of information.

VC Planner Web UI:

Within the VC Planner Web UI, users are empowered to carry out a range of essential tasks and activities.

  • Detailed Capacity Checks: Users can perform in-depth capacity checks at a granular level, ensuring alignment with operational constraints.
  • Forecast Order Analysis: The Web UI enables users to analyze forecasted orders, gaining insights into projected demands and making informed decisions.
  • Assembly Requirements: The VC Planner Web Interface allows users to perform requirements analysis to assess the demand for each assembly or component based on the selected criteria.
  • Restriction Planning: Users have the capability to engage in restriction planning, utilizing predefined rules and constraints to optimize production strategies.

VC Planner Excel UI (Built on SAP IBP):

The VC Planner Excel UI, built on SAP Integrated Business Planning (IBP), serves as a versatile tool for specific planning functions.

  • Demand Planning and Option Planning: Users can effectively engage in demand and option planning activities, aligning strategies with market requirements.
  • Forecast Accuracy: The Excel UI offers tools to assess forecast accuracy, helping users gauge the precision of their predictions.

SAP Analytics Cloud (Optional):

SAP Analytics Cloud is utilized as a user interface for analytics and reporting purposes and is an optional component.

  • /SBPC/IBP_CG (Customer Group Extract)
  • /SBPC/IBP_PRODUCT (Product and Attributes Extract)
  • /SBPC/IBP_BOM (Bill of Materials Extract)
  • /SBPC/IBP_MAT_CR_PLN (Partial Products Extract)
  • /SBPC/IBP_IPPE (IPPE Extract)
  • /SBPC/DERIVED_CHAR (Derived Characteristics Extract)
  • /SBPC/IBP_SH (Sales Order Extract)
  • /SBPC/IBP_CIR_SO_DEL (Delete CIR)

• Location

         Location is synonymous with Plant in ERP. This extract program is used to get all the Locations that are relevant for Planning.

  • Customer Group

          This extract program is used to get the customer group that includes set of customers.

  • Product Information

          This extract is used to extract product, product-location, product-classes, class-characteristics, characteristic values, and product classification

           details.

  • Bill of Materials

         This extract program is used to extract product assemblies, assembly components and BOM object dependencies.

  • Partial Products

         This extract program is used to extract the products that are maintained with specific set of configurations (characteristic values) fixed.

  • iPPE Extracts

         This extract program is used to extract different iPPE nodes, bill of material data, bill of materials, assemblies, assembly components and object         

         dependencies.

  • Derived Characteristics Extract

         This extract program is used to extract rules that are maintained as procedures, constraints, constraints with variant tables.

  • Sales History Extract

         This extract program is used to extract sales order details at header level as well as at configuration level.

The VC Planner Web Interface presents an array of robust features to streamline and enhance the planning process. From generating assembly requirements and planning within constraints to producing forecast orders, it offers a comprehensive suite of tools. This interface facilitates seamless data extraction from ERP systems through job execution, and it extends its utility by enabling data dissemination to various demand and supply planning solutions. With its user-friendly design and versatile capabilities, the VC Planner Web Interface is a pivotal asset for organizations aiming to optimize their planning strategies and achieve supply chain efficiency.

• Location

A location can be defined as a physical site or an organizational entity responsible for the management of product inventories or resources. These sites encompass distribution centers, manufacturing plants, and Demand Locations. These locations typically serve as storage and production hubs for various products, which are subsequently transported to and from various other destinations. This list includes essential categories such as demand locations, planning locations, and factory locations, providing a centralized repository of vital information for effective planning and resource allocation within the VC Planner framework.

The Location Application presents a list of all the locations considered for planning purposes.

  • Location - Product

Location-Product application refers to a list of products that have been designated or associated with a particular location within a supply chain. In this context, it means that the product is primarily stored, managed, or tracked at a specific physical site or organizational unit, such as a warehouse, distribution center, retail store, or manufacturing facility.

  • Configurable Product

A Configurable Product refers to an item or product that can be customized or configured by customers or users based on their specific preferences or requirements. This customization typically involves selecting different features, or options to create a personalized version of the product. The Configurable Product application serves as a application that provides a list of such products that are available for planning purposes.

  • Product Configuration

The Product Configuration application displays the assignment of product classes to configurable items, offering both master and detail page views for efficient management of product attributes and specifications.

  • Customer Group

The Customer Group application showcases the categorization of customers into distinct groups, aiding businesses in implementing targeted marketing strategies and tailored services based on specific customer segments.

  • Bill of Material

The Bill of Material application presents a comprehensive view of product assemblies, highlighting their associated locations, constituent products, and their respective characteristics.

  • Products

This application provides a comprehensive display of product details, encompassing partial products, assemblies, components, and configurable products.

  • Planning Network Maintenance

The Planning Network Maintenance application enables users to visualize the relationships between partial products and their corresponding demand, planning, and factory locations. Users can conveniently map partial products to specific locations within the supply chain.

• BOM Product Variant Structure

The "BOM Product Variant Structure" application provides a visual representation of the product's Bill of Materials (BOM) structure, displaying key BOM nodes and components. This enables users to quickly understand the hierarchical composition of a product variant. Note that VC Planner converts the multi-level BOM to 2 level flat BOM where the 1st level contains the assembly/components directly used in configurable product and the second level represents the materials that are procured from suppliers that falls under the 1st level assembly.

  • Assign Predication Profiles

Planners can assign prediction profiles for a specific Product configuration. These prediction profiles are used in generating predictions based on historical data for each characteristic value.

  • PVS Nodes maintenance
  • Partial Product Configuration

The Partial Product Configuration tile is intended for creating or updating partial product configurations within a configurable product. It allows users to define specific configurations or variations of a product.

  • Prediction Profile Maintenance

Planners can create prediction profiles. These prediction profiles are assigned to a Product Configuration.

  • IBP Characteristic

This application compiles a list of characteristics for a configurable product from the entire set of configurable product characteristics that will be sent to SAP IBP for planning. For example, technical characteristics are deemed irrelevant for planning in IBP; therefore, these will be unchecked and will not be included in the data sent to IBP for the planning process.

  • Class - IBP Characteristics

This application is designed to map characteristics that are predefined as part of Partial Products' definitions and are transmitted to IBP as attributes of the Product Master.

  • Characteristic Prioritization

This application enables planners to prioritize primary characteristics over secondary characteristics of a configurable product. This prioritization aids in forecast consumption, as the system forms clusters with relevant characteristics.

  • New Product Introduction

(Under Development)

  • Critical Assembly

This application provides information about the critical component flag that is included as part of Assembly Components. This flag ensures that components or assemblies marked as critical will be considered for requirements calculations. Additionally, a detailed capacity check can be performed if the component's capacity information is available in the system.

  • Planning Network Maintenance

This tile is designed to show the Demand, Planning and Factory location with respective to the partial products selected.

User has the option to map the Partial Products with Demand, Planning and Factory location.

  • Assembly Components

Assembly Components application displays the list of all Assemblies which are assigned to the Product are displayed.

  • Component Availability

The Component Availability application displays a list of all components for the selected location and their respective capacities within the chosen date range. It also offers options to manually update the capacities or upload a flat file for making mass updates.

• Line Master

The application enables planners to create a Line Master, which serves as the foundation for establishing additional restrictions and parameters in the planning process.

  • Location-Product-Line

This tile is designed to display the location and product along with their respective lines and line descriptions. Used to map the lines with the location and product.

  • Restrictions

This application permits planners to formulate a set of rules for combining various characteristic values and then apply these rules as constraints. Consequently, the system can perform requirement calculations based on these defined restrictions.

  • Restrictions Capacity

This tile has been specifically designed to facilitate the ongoing maintenance of weekly capacity restrictions. The options available permits planners to even upload a flat file for mass maintenance.

  • Restriction Likelihood

This application offers insights into capacity checks and provides details about the demand requirements originating from different location-product combinations based on the specified restriction. It calculates usage and issues alerts for combinations where the capacity falls short of meeting the requirements.

  • Line Capacity

Line Capacity tile is designed to maintain capacity at Line level for a Product.

• Assembly Requirements

This application offers assembly requirements for the chosen manufacturing location, configurable product, IBP version, IBP scenario, and date range. The system takes into account all the BOM component coefficients during the requirement calculation process. It begins with the demand for the main product, checks the rules for assembly selection, and subsequently calculates the requirements.

  • Component Requirements

In the component requirement application, planners can:

    • Check component demand based on configurable product-level demand using the static BOM.
    • Evaluate capacity usage based on available capacity in relation to component demand requirements.
    • Perform detailed disaggregation to the demand location and planning variant levels. This view is available for Quantity, TS Component Coefficient, and Normalization Display Modes.
    • Filter alerted components using a slider bar based on usage percentage, applicable to Quantity and Capacity Usage display modes.
    • Check normalized demand for Planning Variant without considering BOM coefficients.
    • Analyze Time Series-based Component Coefficients to select components per week based on driving options.
  • Forecast Orders

The Forecast Orders application offers a detailed view for the selected Manufacturing Location, Demand Location, Product, and date range. Within this view, planners can observe Forecast Orders at the Unique ID level, providing the most detailed configuration for a configurable product. Additionally, the application provides drill-down views, allowing planners to examine the top 5 closest Unique IDs based on the clustering of characteristics. This feature assists planners in adjusting the Forecast Quantity within the Firm Horizon. Moreover, the application allows planners to publish Forecast Orders to the S4 system if they approve the generated forecast and wish to transmit it as Independent Requirements to the S4 system.

  • Unique Characteristics

This tile is designed to display the Unique Characteristics of the selected Location and Configurable product. This application is divided into two sections: the Master section and the Detail section. The Master section contains a list of Unique IDs, and when one is selected, the detailed screen will present all the characteristics and their associated values.

  • Seed Orders Creation

This tile is designed to create/show seed orders for respective Location and Configurable Product selected. Seed orders are then used for further processing of Predictions and also used to generate planning objects in SAP IBP for maintaining Option Planning for future buckets.

• Job Scheduler

This job scheduler application is designed to view and create the Jobs along with that user can view schedule details, schedule logs, and run logs. Using this application, BTP can pull the data from SAP then process it and send the processed data to IBP and then return the results to SAP.

  • Job Scheduler Log

Job Scheduler Log application displays Job Logs which are created.

• Characteristic Influence

When conducting a detailed capacity check, it's essential to understand the characteristics influencing critical components' requirements. To comprehend the influence of characteristics on a specific component, VC Planner provides an application where users can examine all the characteristics driving component requirements.

All the features and functionality included in the SAP IBP Demand Planning or Time Series-based S&OP planning license are integrated into the VC Planner IBP Features. For specific details about each feature available under the mentioned license, please refer to the standard documentation provided by SAP IBP. Additionally, VC Planner offers a built-in planning area as an integral component of the product implementation, providing users with a comprehensive planning environment.

Note:
The VC Planner planning area will be updated with every SAP IBP release and validated for compatibility. All the new features relevant for planning released under the demand or TS supply modules will automatically become available in VC Planner.

The Consensus Demand is derived from the S&OP (Sales and Operations Planning) Planning area, relying on the Demand plan established during the SOP Demand Review process. This Consensus Demand serves as the initial demand input for initiating the Characteristic-based planning process. In this phase, the system dissects the demand down to the level of Partial Products or Configurable Products and further breaks it down into individual characteristic value levels.

Note:
Transfer of demand to VC Planner can be done either at Location Product level or at Location Product Customer, depending on the supply chain network.

In the Planning process, the Consensus Demand plan is transferred from the IBP S&OP Planning area to the VC Planner Planning area using a configured copy operator within the IBP system.

Once the VCP Planning area receives the demand data, VC Planner utilizes Sales Orders and seed orders to calculate option take rates for other characteristics marked as planning relevant within a fully configured Product. These calculated options take rates are displayed within the VCP Planning area and can be adjusted by planners if needed.

The process of uploading seed orders to the VC Planner system and generating statistical option percentages involves several key steps:

Seed Order Creation and Upload:

  • Seed Orders act as pseudo-sales orders and are used for generating option planning for products without historical sales data.
  • The Seed Order application, located under Planning Functions, enables users to create or upload seed orders for new planning combinations.
  • Users can either download an Excel template and populate it with mandatory data or create orders directly within the VC Planner application.
  • The template includes fields for Location (demand source), Product ID (configurable product reference), and Unique ID (System generated ID based on the fully configured configuration).

Note:
VC Planner provides an application with Unique Characteristics, offering information about characteristics and characteristic values related to the Unique ID. It includes each Unique ID and its validity dates.

Generate Statistical Option Percentage:

  • VC Planner uses the uploaded seed orders or the actual sales orders on the product to calculate statistical option percentages.
  • These percentages can be accessed through the VC Planner Excel UI using the Planning view template.
  • Various statistical forecast models are employed, offering flexibility in determining option percentages based on historical data.

Adjusting Option Percentages:

  • VC Planner provides a manual override option for Planners to adjust option percentages.
  • Manual overrides take precedence over Sales Options % and Statistical Forecast Option %.

Generating Option Percentage:

  • The option percentage is generated based on inputs from Sales Options, Planner overrides, and Statistical Forecast Option %.
  • Manual overrides hold the highest priority, followed by Sales Option % and then the Statistical Forecast Option % generated by the system.

Generating Final Forecast Option %:

  • Using the final option percentage (%), VC Planner generates forecast orders.
  • The system may round forecast orders to the nearest decimal, apply rules for option selection, or allow direct adjustments by planners within the Firm Horizon.
  • These adjustments impact the Option Percentage and trigger VC Planner to recalculate the Final Forecast Option % based on Forecast Orders generated, serving as a reference for planners to understand the final option % considered by the system.

The generation of Forecast Orders for a Configurable Product involves several steps in VC Planner:

  • Import Future Demand: Future demand is imported into BTP along with the Option Plan.
  • Generate Time Series and Predictions: The system then generates time series data and predictions based on predefined rules and authorizations for characteristic values.
  • Combine Predicted Values: Using the predicted values and combining them with Option Planning and Demand data, the detailed configuration for the product is established.
  • Override Forecast Quantity: Planners have the ability to override the Forecast Quantity generated within the Firm Horizon by directly managing detailed level values in BTP.
  • Adjust Forecast in Forecast Horizon: Within the Forecast Horizon, changes to the plan can only be made by adjusting the Option Plan and Demand coming from the SOP system.

Based on the Demand Planned for Partial Products, the system follows these steps:

  • Generate Assembly and Component Requirements: The system generates Assembly requirements and Component requirements based on the static bill of materials and object dependencies. These dependencies define which assemblies or components are selected based on the Option Plan.
  • Perform Detailed Capacity Check: Planners can then perform a detailed capacity check where they compare the available capacity with the requirements generated for components in VC Planner.

A detailed capacity check at the characteristics level, including characteristics and characteristic levels, plays a vital role in the MPS process. This step is carried out using the restrictions planning application in the VC Planner system.

In the VC Planner system, the iPPE structure, along with assembly headers and components, is extracted. Components deemed critical are marked as such in the S4 system's MRP view of the product. VC Planner then extracts these materials alongside the iPPE structure. Object dependencies within the iPPE structure are employed to link components to technical characteristics and their respective values. Variant configuration rules are utilized to map these technical characteristics to sales characteristics. MPS planners can identify sales characteristics suitable for applying restrictions within the restriction planning application.

MPS planners have the flexibility to impose restrictions on single characteristics or use multiple characteristics within a single rule. These restrictions include start and end dates to account for time-sensitive constraints and can be written for specific values or multiple values of the same characteristic using OR conditions.

Subsequently, MPS planners manage capacity for each restriction in weekly buckets. These capacities in weekly intervals are compared against forecast predictions, enabling a detailed capacity check in the VC Planner system.

VC Planner employs an inbuilt algorithm to assess capacities, with planners viewing the results in the restriction likelihood application. Planners can drill down into weekly restrictions' capacity variations by clicking on error records, which provide details on demand location, planning variants, and quantities.

If MPS planners find the displayed results unsatisfactory, they can adjust forecast orders within the VC Planner system's firm horizon or modify option percentages in the VCP Planning area. If these adjustments fail to resolve capacity constraints and volume changes are necessary at the planning variant level, MPS planners collaborate with the demand sales planning team to make adjustments. This triggers a complete restart of the MPS process with the newly adjusted demand. Background jobs manage these adjustments and execute a fresh capacity check.

DESCRIPTION: Analytics and Reporting in VC Planner
CONTENT:
VC Planner offers a range of reports and analytics that are invaluable for exception management, aiding planners in their day-to-day tasks. These reports and visualizations include the following:

  • Sales Orders Reports: These reports provide a detailed view of current and upcoming sales orders. Planners can use this information to ensure that production and supply chains are aligned with customer demand. By analyzing Sales Orders, planners can identify trends, customer preferences, and fluctuations in demand.
  • Forecast Orders Reports: Forecast Orders reports are instrumental in predicting future demand based on historical data and market insights. Planners can assess the accuracy of their forecasts and make necessary adjustments to meet future demand effectively. This information helps in optimizing plans and notifying production team on the changes made based on recent trends.
  • Demand Snapshots: Demand snapshots offer a comprehensive view of the current demand landscape. This includes details on demand by product, location, or specific attributes. Planners can analyze demand patterns, identify high-demand items, and focus on areas that require attention, such as potential stockouts or overstock situations. Snapshots of previous plans can be utilized to compare the current plan vs previous plans to understand the various aspects of markets. Lag based snapshots provides a better understanding of planners KPI and meet better forecast accuracy.

The primary objective of these reports and analytics is to assist planners in understanding and managing Forecast and the overall accuracy of their planning activities. By examining these reports, planners can make data-driven decisions, fine-tune their strategies, and proactively address any exceptions or deviations from the expected plan. This leads to more efficient resource allocation, reduced costs, and improved customer satisfaction through better fulfillment of orders and demand.
VC Planner provides two major outputs for the subsequent planning process, which are discussed as follows:

When performing Supply planning using TS Component Coefficients in the Supply Planning system, VC Planner offers dynamic Component Coefficients that vary according to different option selections within specific time buckets. This data serves as an essential input for TS-Based Heuristic, enabling the generation of Component Usage and facilitating planning for supplier commitments and capacity validations.

Moreover, the utilization of Finite/Optimizer Heuristic allows for the creation of a constrained demand plan that is contingent on material availability. This approach ensures that planning is optimized within the constraints of resource availability.

The final step in the VC Planner system involves the MPS (Master Production Scheduling) planner sending the MPS plan to the S4 system in the form of a CIR (Customer Independent Requirements). This integration is established through a standard ODATA service, triggered when the forecast is published from VC Planner. Before publishing, the planner ensures a detailed capacity check is completed, and the Time Series Component Coefficients for the MPS plan is sent to the IBP S&OP planning area where the supply plan is completed and confirmed by syncing the Constrained Plan with VC Planner.

MPS planners utilize the Forecast Order Fiori application to publish the forecast once all adjustments are made and the plan meets their satisfaction. In this application, planners can view forecast orders, and by clicking the "Publish" button, they initiate the transfer of the forecast to the S4 system. Additionally, if needed, users can click the "Download" button to obtain the forecast data in Excel format for further analysis or documentation. This final step ensures seamless communication between VC Planner and S4, enabling accurate and timely production planning and execution.
